commit_message:
QUIC: 0RTT for gnutls via CURLSSLOPT_EARLYDATA

When a QUIC TLS session announced early data support and
'CURLSSLOPT_EARLYDATA' is set for the transfer, send initial request and
body (up to the 128k we buffer) as 0RTT when curl is built with
ngtcp2+gnutls.

QUIC 0RTT needs not only the TLS session but the QUIC transport
paramters as well. Store those and the earlydata max value together with
the session in the cache.

Add test case for h3 use of this. Enable quic early data in nghttpx for
testing.

Closes #15667

findings.title: Session count read after releasing scache lock in Curl_ssl_scache_take
findings.message: In Curl_ssl_scache_take(), the SSL session cache lock is released via Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) before the trace logging code runs. The trace statement (CURL_TRC_CF / later CURL_TRC_SSLS) calls Curl_llist_count(&peer->sessions) to report how many sessions remain for that peer. Because this happens after the lock has already been released, another thread can concurrently mutate peer->sessions (adding/removing/destroying nodes, or even freeing/expiring the peer entry) between the unlock and the Curl_llist_count() call, resulting in a data race on the shared peer->sessions llist. This can produce an inconsistent/incorrect count in the trace output, and in the worst case (if the peer structure itself is freed by a concurrent scache_put/expire path) it could lead to a use-after-free style read on peer->sessions/peer. The unlock was moved up in front of the trace logic when this function was reworked to add QUIC 0RTT support, splitting what used to be a single 'take then trace' sequence under lock.
findings.suggestion: Move Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) to after the trace logging (i.e., after the entire if(s)/else block that reads peer->sessions), so the lock still protects all reads of the shared peer/session-list state used for the diagnostic count.

ground_truth.root_cause: When Curl_ssl_scache_take() was reworked to add QUIC 0RTT support and richer trace logging, the call to Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) was placed immediately after the critical section that removes/takes a session from the peer's session list, but before the subsequent trace-logging code that itself reads the same shared peer->sessions list (via Curl_llist_count) to report the remaining session count. This left a window where lock-protected data is read/used without holding the lock.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Session count read after releasing scache lock in Curl_ssl_scache_take
